context: Find all paths that start at the root, end at a node with value 7, and contain no 3. The binary tree has 8 nodes. Root 1 has left child 7 and right child 3. The shallow 7 on the left has left child 4 and right child 5, and 4 has a left child with value 7. Node 3 has left child 6 and a 7 on its right. The seven-node input in the earlier example and accompanying Python code lacks the deeper 7 below node 4. On that seven-node tree, removing the return after recording a solution yields no additional solution.

The comparison concerns the return that ends the current recursive branch immediately after recording a solution. Both versions still prune the search at a node with value 3 and backtrack normally after exploring a node's children. The framework code implements this pruning by rejecting choices with value 3.
description: The left panel keeps the early return after recording a solution, and the right panel removes it. The table compares which nodes are visited and which paths are found. In both panels the search stops descending at the red node 3 on the right, skipping 6 and the rightmost 7.

frames.explanation: By continuing past the shallow 7 after recording it, the search in the right panel finds the deeper 7 among its descendants. Ending the branch early misses this solution.
frames.title: When to keep searching after recording a solution

summary: When descendants of a target node may also yield solutions, returning immediately after recording a solution misses deeper ones. Remove the early return to continue searching.

tables.caption: Search behavior and results after recording a solution
rows: Left panel: keep the early return
Stop at the shallow 7, skipping its descendants 4, 5, and the deeper 7
Right panel: remove the early return
After recording the shallow 7, visit 4, the deeper 7, and then 5
